chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Muhammad bin Yahya, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who killed his mother, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He does not inherit her, and he is killed due to it in humiliation, and I do not think that his being killed due to it is an expiation for his sin.'

key_terms.يَرِثُهَا: He inherits her (referring to the killer inheriting from the victim)
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ بِهَا: He is killed due to it (execution for the murder)

ai.seo_question: Does a killer inherit from the person he killed, and is his execution an expiation for the sin?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that a man who kills his mother is excluded from inheriting her estate, with his execution carried out in a humiliating manner (ṣāghiran). Furthermore, this execution itself is not considered a divine expiation (kaffarah) for the sin of matricide, highlighting the unique gravity of killing one's mother in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that while inheritance rights are forfeited, the punishment remains distinct from spiritual absolution.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws regarding a man who killed his mother. Heasws said: ‘He would not inherit her, and he would be killed humiliatingly due to it, and Iasws do not think that his being killed due to it is an expiation (kaffara) for his sin’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab fn abu ‘ Ubaydah who has narrated the following: “About the case of a man who kills his mother, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He cannot inherit from her. Instead he is executed against his wishes and I do not think that his execution can remedy his sin.’”
